result.title: Linear Bandits under Exact Sliding-Window Constraints
result.comment: 53 pages, including supplementary material; 8 figures and 6 tables
result.summary: We study linear bandits under exact sliding-window constraints, where every consecutive block of actions must belong to a prescribed feasible set. In the offline setting, where the reward function is known, we show that convexity and cyclic-shift invariance make a stationary solution optimal when $w\mid T$ and within an additive $O(w)$ gap otherwise. In the online setting, we show that geometric structure alone is insufficient for learning, and sublinear regret can be impossible. We introduce a transition diameter $τ$ that quantifies feasible reachability and develop a rare-switching OFUL algorithm with regret $\widetilde{O}(d\sqrt{T}+τd+w)$ against the offline-optimal feasible trajectory. Finally, we remove cyclic invariance and consider general sliding-window constraints, where optimal behavior may be non-stationary. We represent recent action history as the state of a finite-memory control problem and introduce a history-state diameter $D$ that measures feasible communication between viable histories. Combining optimistic remaining-horizon planning with rare policy updates, we obtain a regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(d\sqrt{T}+dD+w)$. We evaluate our approach on real-world and synthetic benchmarks, showing that it maintains exact feasibility while achieving reward and regret comparable to baselines with substantially fewer policy updates.

AI.brief_summary: 研究精确滑动窗口约束下的线性 bandit：离线已知奖励时证明凸性与循环平移不变性使平稳解最优，在线情形指出仅有几何结构不足以学习、次线性 regret 可能不可达，并引入 transition diameter 与 rare-switching OFUL 算法；进一步把最近动作历史视为有限记忆控制问题的状态，用 history-state diameter 刻画可行历史间的可达性。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 的潜在联系在于用「历史状态 + 可达性直径」刻画决策过程的可通信性，可能为 latent 推理中动态计算分配、停止决策与证据获取成本提供形式化视角，供核查其状态抽象与切换代价分析能否迁移到多模态推理轨迹的评价。
